text:
I treated each prompt as a separate chance for an app name to appear anywhere in the answer. Broad requests such as “for students,” “for work,” or “best app” can prompt comparisons across several apps; device and feature constraints make mentions more selective. The two prompts that name Goodnotes or Notability can also elicit competitor comparisons.

The feature associations support different mention patterns: OneNote is a cross-platform option with handwriting and handwriting-to-text features; Goodnotes is strongly associated with stylus and handwriting use, including Android and Windows; Notability is associated with handwritten notes and audio recording or transcription. Notion fits work, research, and Claude-integration queries, while Otter is most likely on lecture, meeting, recording, and dictation prompts. [Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/onenote/onenote-help-and-learning/take-handwritten-notes-in-onenote), [Goodnotes Support](https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/articles/7922907940367-Frequently-requested-features-for-Android-Windows-and-Web), [Notability](https://notability.com/meetings), [Notion Help](https://www.notion.com/help/notion-mcp), [Otter Help](https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/4425393298327-Otter-Notetaker-Overview)

These are estimated per-question mention rates across the full 100-query set, not market shares or recommendation rates.

text:
These are estimated name-mention rates across all 100 questions. I count an app whenever a plausible answer would mention it, including as an alternative or in response to a prompt that names it directly.

The strongest triggers are the platform and feature constraints: OneNote fits Microsoft, Android, and free-use prompts; Goodnotes and Notability fit stylus, iPad, and handwriting prompts; Notion fits work, research, and organization prompts; Otter fits lecture and meeting transcription prompts. Official product materials confirm these associations—for example, OneNote supports handwritten notes, Goodnotes supports handwriting-to-text across platforms, Notability offers meeting transcription, and Notion offers AI meeting notes. ([Microsoft Support](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/onenote/take-handwritten-notes-in-onenote-for-android), [Goodnotes Support](https://support.goodnotes.com/hc/en-us/articles/7922907940367-Frequently-requested-features-for-Android-Windows-and-Web), [Notability](https://notability.com/meetings), [Notion](https://www.notion.com/help/ai-meeting-notes))

The estimates also account for prompts where these apps are poor fits: unusual device or game queries, Bible study, and Apple Watch requests. Overall, Notion and OneNote have the broadest likely reach; Goodnotes and Notability are concentrated in handwriting and tablet prompts, while Otter is concentrated in audio and meeting prompts.
